chapter_theme: Testing friends before committing, because a friendship once formed should not be left. It asks what to test for, finds that ruin is the most reliable test, and accepts that bad friendships must sometimes be paid to end.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar: the harm of not testing (791-792), how to test and whom to choose (793-796), whom not to befriend (797-799), and a summary of both (800).

791.reading: Nothing brings ruin like befriending without inquiry, since for those devoted to friendship there is no leaving once it is formed.
791.nuance: The logic turns on faithfulness: the reason for caution is precisely the commitment to stay. Parimelazhagar adds that with no distinction between friends, the friend's sins and blame become one's own.

792.reading: The friendship of one who does not inquire again and again ends by bringing grief that kills him.
792.nuance: The doubled ஆய்ந்தாய்ந்து asks for repeated testing and not a single check. For Parimelazhagar no enemy is needed, for one brings it on oneself, and the bad friend's enemies become one's own.

793.reading: Know his qualities, his family, his faults and his inan, and only then form a friendship.
793.nuance: Faults are on the list to be known, not to be absent. Parimelazhagar's point is that no one is faultless, so the question is whether the faults can be borne.

positions.position: குன்றா இனன் is a friend's undiminished kin, since those bound to kin bring that bond along with them.
The phrase means qualities that don't decline, not relatives.

794.reading: One of good family who feels shame at blame on himself: that friendship should be had even by giving.
794.nuance: பழிநாணுவான் is a person who is governed by shame. The commercial phrase is startling for something the previous chapter praises so highly. Kalaignar softens it to 'by any means', while Parimelazhagar says plainly: buy it for a price.

795.reading: Inquire and take the friendship of those able to speak until one weeps, to rebuke, and to teach what is proper.

positions.position: The verse describes friends, who dissuade before the act, press hard after it, and make one do what is proper.
positions.quote: தாம் உலக வழக்கல்லது செய்யக் கருதின்சோகம் பிறக்கும்வகை சொல்லி விலக்கியும்

positions.position: The verse is about which ministers a ruler should befriend.

796.reading: Even in ruin there is one benefit: it is a rod that measures one's people to full length.
796.nuance: The benefit is knowledge rather than comfort. Parimelazhagar says the true extent of each friend's bond stays hidden in wealthy times, and that ruin measures it for choosing better afterward.

797.reading: Gain for a person means giving up and leaving the friendship of fools.
797.nuance: The verse calls a loss a gain. Parimelazhagar says one must also move away, because like sandal and vengai burning together, nearness alone brings harm.

798.reading: Do not think on what shrinks the spirit, and do not take the friendship of those who cut away in distress.
798.nuance: The verse pairs a rule about thought and a rule about company, and Parimelazhagar treats the first as an illustration of the second. Fair-weather friends are thus a thing that shrinks the mind.

799.reading: Friendship with those who forsake one in ruin burns the heart, even to think of, at the moment of death.
799.nuance: Betrayal is measured against death and is what burns. Parimelazhagar goes further: the mere thought of it is worse than Death, and even for an unconnected person who thinks of it. He also records another reading in which the thought is of the harm one brought on oneself.

800.reading: Keep close to the friendship of the stainless; give something if you must, but leave the friendship of those who are oppilar.
800.nuance: The cost of a bad friendship is paid at the end as well. It balances 794: one may pay to get a friend and pay to be rid of one.

positions.position: ஒப்பிலார் are those out of accord with the world.
ஒப்பிலார் are those not one's equals.
They are simply those who carry a stain, the contrary of the first half.

links.note: 791 demands inquiry before a friendship begins. 796 says ruin is what truly measures friends, and Manakkudavar adds it is hard to know them otherwise. So the test that matters most can't be run in advance, and this undercuts the chapter's own program.

791 says those devoted to friendship cannot leave a friend once made. 797 calls leaving a fool's friendship pure gain. Parimelazhagar's 800 offers a way out: leaving is for what one took on without knowing.

793 and 794 screen friends by family. 972 says birth is equal for all living beings and only deeds make the difference. The chapter on choosing friends keeps a criterion that the chapter on greatness dissolves.

source_issues: 797: Parimelazhagar's விளக்கம் is garbled, with a stray § and a repeated passage.
